generatedCommentsNodes.comment: Minor: `creationCheck.set((false))` has redundant double parentheses around `false`. This is harmless but inconsistent with the surrounding style (e.g., the `else` branch uses `creationCheck.set(false)`).

The log message still reads `"rolling over data stream [{}] lazily as a followup to the upgrade of the [{}] index template [{}]"`, but the behavior now also covers initial installation (as made explicit by the renamed method and updated Javadoc in #ZRH13). The word "upgrade" is misleading in the installation case; consider "update" or "installation/update" to stay consistent with the new semantics.

When `dsTemplateName` is `null` (i.e., `findV2Template` found no matching template for the data stream), the code falls through to `metadata.templatesV2().get(null)`, which returns `null`, making `dsTemplate == null` true. The condition then reduces to `indexTemplate.priorityOrZero() > 0`. For a template with no explicit priority (the common default), `priorityOrZero()` returns `0`, so the expression is `false` and the data stream is excluded from rollover. However, if no existing template matches the data stream, the newly installed template is by definition the first (and only) matching template, so it should trigger rollover regardless of its priority value. Consider treating the `dsTemplate == null` case as an unconditional `true` (or at least decoupling it from the priority comparison).

review_comment: IIUC, for other plugins (like otel-data plugin) that are using IndexTemplateRegistry this would be a no-op since there would be no datastreams to apply rollover too -- Is this correct? Maybe we should have a test to assert this behavior as a follow-up i.e. check if `rollover_on_write` flag is `false` for a datastream created after the plugin is installed?

I'm not sure I understand the scenario. Do you mean a negative check, verifying something that does not match the index pattern is rolled over? I think the existing `IndexTemplateRegistryTests.testAutomaticRollover` covers that: it creates two logs and one traces data stream, and verifies that only the logs ones are rolled over when updating the logs template.

Not exactly a negative check -- my concern is when plugins operate under normal circumstances then there is no need to rollover on installation. I was thinking of having a test case to cover this scenario to make sure that rollover on installation doesn't break anything for other plugins. Does it make sense?
